questions.q: What do we call a closed figure made of exactly five straight line segments?
questions.a: It is called a pentagon. A student who says "square" or "triangle" has not yet learned the naming convention based on side counts, indicating a need to review the list of polygon names.

questions.q: If a quadrilateral has all sides equal but its corners are not the same size, is it a regular polygon? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is not regular. To be regular, both sides AND angles must be equal; a student who says "yes" assumes that equal sides alone define a regular polygon, missing the requirement for equal angles.

questions.q: A shape has 6 sides of different lengths and different angles. Is it a polygon? If so, what is it called?
questions.a: Yes, it is a hexagon. A student who says "it is not a polygon" confuses "irregular" with "not a polygon." A polygon only requires straight, closed segments, regardless of whether they are equal.

questions.q: Compare an equilateral triangle and a scalene triangle. Which one is a regular polygon and why?
questions.a: The equilateral triangle is regular because all sides and all angles are equal. A student who struggles here fails to connect the definition of "regular" to the specific properties of geometric shapes.

questions.q: If you are asked to draw an irregular octagon, what is the one rule you must follow to ensure it is still a polygon?
questions.a: You must ensure it has exactly eight straight sides and that the figure is closed. A student who says "all sides must be equal" has confused the definition of a general polygon with that of a regular one.

questions.q: Draw a shape that is NOT a polygon and explain why it fails the definition.
questions.a: Accept any shape with a curved line or an open end (e.g., a circle or a "C" shape). Failure to include a curve or an opening indicates the student doesn't grasp the "straight line segments" or "closed" criteria.
